# S04 — Engine for one implementer: setup, implement, checks, review, gate, approve, commit, ledger

The slice state machine for one slice, run against a fake role runner:
setup, implement, checks, review, gate, awaiting approval, commit, with the
ledger, run records and restart reconcile (`plan.s04-cut`). Claude is the
only vendor; the real adapter is S16 and the owner surface is S17.

**Not in this slice:** budgets, fallback, codex or grok, waves, the TUI, socket methods or CLI commands (S05, S06, S16, S17).

## Why

Every later engine slice (waves, vendors, live detail, landing) builds on
this state machine. Built against a fake runner, it can be tested without
any vendor call and in parallel with S16.

## Files

- `internal/engine/` (new): the state machine, briefs, report checks,
  permission resolution, and a `Runner` interface for one role round
  (input: role, round, vendor, model, effort, brief, worktree, report path,
  allowlist or read-only, resume session; output: exit class, session,
  report text, tokens, cost, permission denials).
- `internal/runrec/` (new): `run.json` per run under
  `~/.local/state/ork/runs/<run>/`, atomic writes, `writes[]`, retention
  (docs/state.md).
- `internal/slicercli/`: the write calls the engine needs (`relay-run
  begin|step|end`, `note`, `check --json`, `relay-roles recommend --json`),
  each recorded in `writes[]` and retried on `locked`.
- `internal/roles/`: the accepted contract set, and the owner-question
  wording from the S10 note.
- `internal/cli/doctor.go`: check against the accepted set.
- Not `internal/daemon`, `internal/ipc`, `internal/tui` or a vendor
  adapter (S15, S16, S17).

## Failing tests

- A run goes setup, implement, checks, review, gate (lite, resumed
  reviewer), awaiting approval; on approve it commits with the slice's Git
  title and no attribution, then runs the finish step the contract orders.
- Setup runs `git worktree add` with the registry's patterns, adds
  `.worktrees/` to `info/exclude` when missing, and `slicer relay-run
  begin`; every role round is a ledger step with `--parent` on the
  orchestrator step ork owns, and its phase is set on exit.
- Red checks send the implementer back with the failing output and spend
  no review. Review findings start a fix round; a gate FAIL is noted with
  `slicer note ID --text "Review FAIL: ..."`; a third FAIL stops the slice.
- Report checks: the gate's first line must be exactly `VERDICT: PASS` or
  `VERDICT: FAIL`; a missing `Tests:` line or `## Owner needed` section is
  an error the owner sees (`role.report-shape`). A non-empty Owner needed
  pauses the slice with the question; an answer resumes the role with it.
- Stop rules: an exit not classified ok, a permission denial, a read-only
  role that changed the tree (`git status --porcelain` before and after),
  and a lost process each stop or pause the slice with the reason.
- The implementer's allowlist is the registry's `permissions.implementer`,
  else the built-in default: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, `Bash(slicer
  *)`, `Bash(git status*)`, `Bash(git diff*)`, `Bash(git log*)` and
  `Bash(<check command>*)` (`launch.default-allowlist`). Read-only roles
  get read-only mode.
- Restart: loading run records with a role whose process group is gone, or
  alive but not attached, kills it if alive, marks it lost and pauses the
  slice in needs-you; the owner can retry that role or stop
  (`engine.restart`).
- `writes[]` holds every slicer, adj and git write with argv, root, exit,
  code, retry and ms; a `locked` exit is retried with backoff and each retry
  is logged (`state.writes`).
- The contract check accepts any version in the accepted set ({7}) and
  refuses others, in the engine and in doctor (`boundary.contract`).
- Fake runner, fake slicer, adj and git (internal/clitest), fake clock; no
  real CLI or vendor.

## Implement

- `adj ask` for owner questions, when filed, runs only in the project's
  main checkout (integration review R6); filing itself is S06.
- The orchestrator step is ork's own: agent `ork`, vendor and model empty.
- Budgets, fallback, other vendors, waves and the TUI are later slices.
